newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi to invest $117 bln on power over 25 years.
newsitem.headline: Saudi to invest $117 bln on power over 25 years.

text.p: Saudi Arabia plans to invest 438 billion riyals ($117 billion) on electricity projects over the next 25 years taking its generation capacity to 70,000 megawatts, a cabinet minister was quoted on Monday as saying.

Industry and Electricity Minister Hashem bin Abdullah bin Hashem Yamani said the ministry had completed a plan on power needs in the next 25 years which "includes building transmission networks throughout the kingdom to establish an electric grid linking all parts of the country and the plan would require an investment of around 438 billion riyals".

The minister, whose remarks were published in Saudi papers, said Saudi Arabia planned to invest 138.6 billion riyals in urgently needed projects over the coming five years for the production, transmission and distribution of electricity.

Current power generation capacity is estimated at around 20,000 MW, up from 18,238 in 1994/95. The government expects peak electricity consumption to reach 23,310 MW by the end of the decade from 17,228 MW in 1994/95.
To meet this demand, the government is planning to raise generation capacity to 25,273 MW in 2000.
